decision_checks.check: test net expectancy 95% interval entirely above 0
signal minus random-date control, 95% interval entirely above 0
test expectancy without the top 1% of winners > 0

controls.all_reports: every report with a reported EPS and estimate that meets the liquidity rule, direction = sign of the surprise, no surprise or reaction threshold (what the thresholds add)
controls.random_date: for each signal a random session of the same symbol (not within 15 sessions of any report), same direction, same entry convention and exit

data_guard.window: the 25 sessions before the report session (information known at the signal; nothing after the signal is used to include or exclude a trade)

decision_rule.multiple_testing: 1 strategy x 2 directions x 2 hold caps x 3 costs were looked at; only the primary cell decides, the rest is reported as context.
decision_rule.otherwise: NO_EDGE_DEMONSTRATED (or INSUFFICIENT_DATA when n_test < 150). PASS only authorises a forward SHADOW run; it is never a trading claim.
pass_for_forward_shadow_requires_all: net expectancy > 0 with the month-block bootstrap 95% interval entirely above 0
expectancy minus the random-date control > 0 with its 95% interval entirely above 0
net expectancy on the TRAIN period > 0 (same sign)
the result is not carried by a handful of trades: expectancy without the top 1% of winners is still > 0
decision_rule.primary_cell: test period, both directions pooled, max_hold 20, 20 bps round trip, standardised R

spec.direction: sign of the surprise: positive -> long, negative -> short

reaction.window: close of the last session before the report date -> close of the first session after the report session (the report session is the first session on or after the report date)

event.source: earnings_calendar rows with a reported EPS and an estimate (yfinance; research grade C: not point-in-time, report time of day unknown)

exit.initial_risk: 2 x ATR14 at the signal bar (1R)

spec.hypothesis: After an earnings report whose surprise and first price reaction agree, the stock keeps drifting in that direction over the following weeks by more than costs.
spec.position_rule: at most one open position per (symbol, direction)
spec.signal: close of the reaction window's last session; the position is entered at the OPEN of the next session (the same convention as every other strategy here)

split.purge: a train signal whose position is still open at test_start is dropped from train
